message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to cancel a date because I'm really tired. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we had our first date a week after we started talking. That went well, and then we had our second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday, and we were supposed to have our third date tonight to watch a movie. On the second date, I mentioned that some of the things she said over the last week had been a bit overwhelming, especially since she was planning things way ahead. I just wanted to be honest and let her know that I wanted to take things slow, and she understood that. We made plans to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie, which would have been our third date. I've had an incredibly long week. I barely slept, only getting about four hours of sleep, and I worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. I was really exhausted. When he asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself, I told him I felt horrible but I was absolutely shattered and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do it on Sunday instead, and I said I'd take him out to lunch and pay for it, and we could watch a movie. Since then, I haven't received a response from him. Now I'm worried that after him thinking I wanted out of the relationship, plus me canceling the date, he might think I'm not interested anymore. Is it AITA (Acting in Total Apathy) for me to reschedule the date when he already has doubts about me? Alright, so I need to break this down. First, I need to understand what AITA means in this context. From what I know, AITA is often used in online discussions to describe situations where someone's actions are perceived as apathetic or uncaring, even if they didn't intend to be. So, in this case, is canceling the date because I'm tired seen as AITA? I think it's important to consider the context. I've had a really tough week, working long hours with little sleep. It's understandable that I'm exhausted. I communicated my feelings honestly, letting him know that I was shattered and wouldn't be able to enjoy the date. I also offered to reschedule for Sunday, which shows that I still want to spend time with him, just not tonight. However, I'm worried that by canceling the date, especially after already expressing that I wanted to take things slow, he might think I'm not interested anymore. That could reinforce any doubts he already had about the relationship. I also need to think about how I communicated the cancellation. I told him I felt horrible and explained my exhaustion. I didn't just cancel without any explanation, which is a good thing. I also offered an alternative date, showing that I'm still willing to make an effort. On the other hand, maybe he feels that I'm not prioritizing our time together, especially if he's already had doubts. He might interpret the cancellation as a lack of interest or commitment, even though that's not the case. I also need to consider the dynamics of the relationship so far. We've only been dating for two weeks, and we've had two successful dates. I mentioned wanting to take things slow, which he understood. So, there's a foundation of communication and understanding. But now, with the cancellation, there's a risk of creating uncertainty or doubt in his mind. He might wonder if I'm really interested in moving forward, especially if he's already had some doubts. I also need to think about how I feel about the situation. Am I truly too exhausted to enjoy the date, or am I using tiredness as an excuse to avoid something deeper? It's important to be honest with myself about my motivations. If I'm genuinely too tired, then it's reasonable to reschedule. But if I'm avoiding the date because of anxiety or other reasons, then that's something I need to address. Another thing to consider is the balance of effort in the relationship. If I'm the one initiating the dates and making plans, and I'm the one canceling, it might give the impression that I'm not as invested. But in this case, we made plans together, so it's a mutual decision to reschedule. I also need to think about how he might feel about the cancellation. If he's already had doubts, this could reinforce them. But if he's understanding and communicative, he might appreciate that I'm honest about my limitations. In the end, communication is key. I should probably reach out to him again, apologize for the late response, and reassure him that I still want to spend time with him. I can explain that I was exhausted and that I value our time together. So, to sum up, is it AITA to cancel a date because I'm tired when he already has doubts about me? It depends on how I communicate the cancellation and whether I make an effort to reschedule. If I handle it respectfully and communicate my feelings honestly, it's not AITA. However, if I cancel without explanation or effort to make it up, then it could be seen as AITA. I think the important takeaway is to prioritize clear communication and to show that I still value the relationship, even if I need to reschedule due to exhaustion.
